title: Microbatch livelock detection checklist and on-call diary
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working note for on-call and SRE engineers to detect, triage, and mitigate a class of incidents we've been seeing in the serving runtime where microbatch aggregation + async prefetch/eviction interactions lead to a livelock: throughput collapses, hosts spin CPU, memory climbs or appears "OOM-like" (no single allocation spike), and KV cache churn is extreme. This doc is intentionally lightweight — a checklist + quick commands + diary snippets to capture what we tried during an on-call shift.

Quick symptom profile (how these incidents usually present):
- Client requests queue up; P95/P99 latency jumps while P50 may remain okay for short windows.
- batch_queue_size grows steadily on affected hosts; continuous batching timers reset frequently without progress.
- host process CPU high but not attributed to user goroutines that make forward progress.
- heap/resident memory rises gradually (not a single allocation), eviction counters oscillate rapidly.
- logs show repeated prefetch attempts / eviction retries and many short-lived KV evict/insert operations.
- sometimes manifests as true OOM on a host after prolonged period.

Initial triage timeline template (fill during incident):
- T0: alert fired (alert name, metric, threshold)
- T+2m: confirmed scope (hosts, AZs, tenant impact)
- T+6m: hypothesis and first mitigation attempt (what was toggled)
- T+15m: results of mitigation, next steps or rollback
- T+60m: remediation and postmortem owner assigned

Telemetry & queries to run (PromQL examples):
- batch_queue_depth by host: sum(batch_queue_size) by (host)
- batch_enqueue_rate: rate(serving_batch_enqueue_total[1m])
- batch_dispatch_rate: rate(serving_batch_dispatch_total[1m])
- host_heap_bytes: node_memory_Active_bytes{job="serving-host"} or process_resident_memory_bytes
- kv_evictions/sec: rate(kv_cache_evictions_total[5m])
- prefetch_active_tasks: serving_prefetch_active_tasks
- batch_latency_p99: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(serving_batch_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))

Alert triage thresholds (sensible starting points):
- sustained batch_queue_depth > 200 on > 5 hosts in a pool for 5m
- kv_evictions/sec > 500 for 5m and rising
- host_heap_bytes growth > 10% over 10m on multiple hosts
- batch_dispatch_rate << batch_enqueue_rate for > 2m

Live diagnostic commands (kubectl / host):
- Get affected runtime pods: kubectl get pods -n serving -l pool=<pool-name> -o wide
- Tail runtime logs (multi-host): kubectl logs -n serving <pod> -c runtime --since=15m | egrep "PREFETCH|EVICT|BATCH|deadlock|stall|KV" --color=always
- Check for batch loop resets: kubectl exec -n serving <pod> -- grep -E "batch_timer_reset|batch_accumulate" /var/log/runtime.log | tail -n 200
- Snapshot thread stacks: kubectl exec -n serving <pod> -- kill -SIGQUIT <pid> && kubectl logs -n serving <pod> --tail=200 | sed -n '/=== STACKTRACE ===/,/=== END STACKTRACE ===/p'
- Host-level: ssh to host node, run top/htop, sudo perf top (if allowed), check dmesg for OOM killer

Useful log patterns to grep for (examples from past incidents):
- "prefetch: starting requiester .* attempt=\d+"
- "evict: iterator yielded 0 entries, retrying"
- "batch: dispatch aborted - no ready workers"
- "kv-cache: insert failed, evicting oldest"
- "host-runloop: stall detected, last-progress-ts="

Short-term mitigations (fast, reversible) — try in order and observe 5-10 minutes:
1) Disable prefetching for affected pool(s) (hotfix flag): set runtime.config.pool.<pool>.prefetch.enabled=false and roll config; expected: reduces background KV churn and should lower CPU.
2) Reduce microbatch aggregation window: runtime.config.pool.<pool>.batch.max_delay_ms = 20 -> 5ms; expected: smaller batches, less time for queues to grow; may increase token cost.
3) Throttle eviction path: runtime.config.kv.eviction.throttle_ms = 50 -> 200; expected: slow down eviction churn and reduce lock contention.
4) Route traffic away: disable pool in traffic router or scale down pool size to zero for quick containment.
5) Fallback model variant: route to a less-optimized/more-isolated model instance until root cause fixed.

When NOT to restart hosts:
- If CPU is high but there is evidence of GC and steady memory reclamation, restarting may be disruptive. Prefer toggles above first.
- Restart if host unresponsive to signals, healthchecks failing, or memory trending to > 95% and eviction counters flat (stuck).

Escalation steps (if mitigations fail):
- Tag SRE pager with @oncall-eng and @serving-runtime channel in Slack; paste the triage snippet and top 5 log lines.
- Open a high-priority Jira (SRE-1427 is an example) and attach stacks, perf samples, and Prom queries.
- Consider temporary capacity isolation: move critical tenants to dedicated pool.

Post-incident follow-ups (owner should be assigned during incident):
- Add explicit metrics for prefetch queue length and per-prefetch-task latency.
- Instrument per-host "batch-progress" heartbeat emitted on dispatch success to detect stalls quickly.
- Implement a prefetch circuit breaker: if prefetch failure rate > X for Y seconds, backoff and stop prefetch on that host for Zs.
- Add safe defaults: enforce a hard cap on concurrent prefetch tasks per host.
- Run a chaos test that simulates eviction slowdowns during peak batch load to reproduce.

Notes-to-self (observations from last two incidents):
- When eviction design used blocking file-backed iterators, the host runloop waited on iterator locks, and batch dispatch timers kept resetting. This produced long-lived busy loops with little forward progress.
- A combination of aggressive prefetch and small eviction window exacerbates the oscillation: prefetch populates KV -> eviction aggressively sweeps -> prefetch retries -> tight lock cycles.
- In one case, simply increasing eviction throttle by 5x dropped batch latency and CPU within 4 minutes.

Example on-call diary snippet (real-ish):
- 2025-02-14 03:03 UTC: Alert SRE-BATCH-QUEUE fired for pool=prod-gpu-1; 8 hosts affected.
- 03:05: confirmed queue growth correlates with kv_evictions/sec spike.
- 03:09: toggled prefetch=false for affected pool (flag push); within 6m eviction rate fell 70%, CPU normalized.
- 03:22: rolled forward with eviction throttle bump and lock instrumentation added to next canary.
- Follow-up: owner assigned @Maya Patel to write postmortem and design prefetch circuit breaker.

Open questions / hypotheses to test in postmortem:
- Is the root cause an ordering bug in the eviction iterator that occasionally returns empty sets due to concurrent resize?
- Would changing to a try-lock-based iterator vs blocking iterator reduce runloop stalls?
- How does NUMA and host affinity affect this pattern (we saw amplification on NUMA-bound hosts)?

Attachments & links (for runbook):
- Jira: SRE-1427 (incident tracking)
- PR: serving-runtime/#3987 (eviction-throttle-proto)
- Confluence: "serving-runtime livelock investigations" page (instrumentation plan)

Immediate TODOs after incident closed:
- Add alert: service:batch-progress-heartbeat missing > 2m -> page
- Add dashboard: per-host batch_progress, prefetch_task_count, kv_eviction_rate, batch_latency_p99
- Ship a small experiment: prefetch disabled by default for 24h for one batch pool and measure P99

If you're oncall and unsure, the simplest safe action that often helps is: 1) disable prefetch for the pool, 2) throttle eviction, 3) move traffic. Document results and escalate if not resolved.

-- Riley (oncall notes and checklist)
